description: {image:minecraft:textures/item/writable_book.png width:48 height:48 align:center}
&6&lTHE ISLAND NEEDS A MEMORY
&fAn island becomes home when useful work survives the person who started it.
&fSeason One turns faction identity, public works, rivalries, and records into reasons to return.
&eRead the three reference clauses around this page, then sign the short charter below.&f They separate real hard protections from rules that only work because friends agree to honor them.
&8Leave behind something a later player can use.

quests.title: OPEN THE ISLAND CHARTER

description: {image:minecraft:textures/item/filled_map.png width:48 height:48 align:center}
&a&lBUILD WHERE THE WORLD REMEMBERS
&fHomes, faction halls, markets, roads, memorials, public machines, and lore sites belong only on land the host has explicitly confirmed permanent.
&fAny announced reset zone is an expedition site, not a place for irreplaceable work. Claims are hard boundaries only where the live FTB Chunks configuration really enforces them.
&cNo prank, theft, faction stunt, or contract overrides another team's protected claim or explicit consent.
&8If the reset eats your cathedral, the cathedral was camping.
quests.subtitle: [OPTIONAL REFERENCE] Permanent work needs a boundary that actually means something.

tasks.title: I Know the Permanent-Land and Claim Rule

quests.title: LAND, CLAIMS, AND RESET ZONES

description: {image:minecraft:textures/item/firework_rocket.png width:48 height:48 align:center}
&d&lTHE FUNNY WAR CLAUSE
&fVampires and Hunters may compete through banners, mascots, markets, races, scavenger hunts, public challenges, expeditions, ward demonstrations, architecture, and reversible wilderness mischief.
&fNeutrals may trade, mediate, scout, judge, rescue, courier, host, or sell services to either side without becoming a consolation faction.
&cNo claim intrusion, theft, spawn camping, targeted harassment, irreversible sabotage, or destruction wearing a comedy moustache.
&fCombat is a scheduled opt-in event only, with a host, backup, stop condition, protected noncombatants, and rebuild plan. Winning never grants progression power.
&8A prank with a cleanup crew is a bit. A crater is an incident.
quests.subtitle: [OPTIONAL REFERENCE] Make stories, not support tickets.

tasks.title: I Accept the Rivalry and Optional-Combat Boundary

quests.title: RIVALRY, NEUTRALS, AND OPTIONAL COMBAT

description: {image:vampirism:textures/item/vampire_fang.png width:48 height:48 align:center}
&6&lONE BODY, ONE PARTY, TWO KINDS OF ALLEGIANCE
&fVampirism now provides real Vampire and Hunter factions. FTB Teams provides shared quest progress and FTB Chunks ownership. Season One uses both, but it does not automatically synchronize them.
&eA Vampirism advancement records that an event happened; it is not a live faction-state detector forever.
&fBefore a faction team claims shared foundation supplies, one teammate or the host confirms that the team is presently aligned with that faction.
&fAsk the host before joining, leaving, or switching an FTB party. Claims, storage, contracts, and quest history must be checked rather than guessed.
&8The bureaucracy has developed fangs.
quests.subtitle: [OPTIONAL REFERENCE] Two faction systems exist. Do not pretend they are the same database.

tasks.title: I Understand Vampirism Faction vs FTB Team State

quests.title: VAMPIRISM, FTB TEAMS, AND SWITCHING

description: {image:minecraft:textures/item/writable_book.png width:48 height:48 align:center}
&6&lTHE FOUR-LINE VERSION
&f1. Build irreplaceable work only on confirmed permanent land.
&f2. Claims and consent outrank rivalry, contracts, and bits.
&f3. Combat is optional, scheduled, supervised, and reversible.
&f4. Vampirism faction state and FTB team state are separate; switches need a quick host review.
&7Lore:&f Nessa Quill signs as courier because Greybridge taught her that an agreement nobody can find is only a rumour.
&eObjective:&f Inspect one lantern, then sign the charter after reading the boundary clauses.
&aStandard:&f The lantern inspection is a non-consuming preview; the checkmark records the human review.
&6Starter nudge:&f one Compass and eight Torches.
quests.subtitle: Inspect one lantern, then sign the charter; claims remain dependency-locked.

description: {image:minecraft:textures/item/compass_16.png width:48 height:48 align:center}
&6&lTHREE LEGITIMATE WAYS TO BELONG
&4Vampires&f gain a real supernatural progression and are asked to turn that identity into hospitality, ritual spaces, night infrastructure, and civic obligations.
&bHunters&f gain their own real progression and are asked to turn vigilance into safe roads, public knowledge, workshops, and reliable refuge.
&aNeutrals&f remain human/non-aligned and become the connective tissue: trade, contracts, mapping, MCA civic life, rescue, logistics, and arbitration.
&eNothing here is permanent.&f Switching is allowed, but it creates social and claim bookkeeping. Pick the role you actually want to play this week, not the reward you think is numerically best.
&8The Atlas has stopped pretending the word 'faction' is metaphorical.

chapters.title: VvH 05 · The Work Each Hand Knows

description: {image:minecraft:textures/item/lantern.png width:48 height:48 align:center}
&6&lLORE
&fGreybridge failed for practical reasons: routes had no owner, refuges had no honest capacity, and three records described the same disaster differently.
&fNessa wants the island's existing works linked before contradiction becomes infrastructure. Mirelle calls a findable route the first rescue.
&fElias calls a record that survives its author the first rescue.
&e&lOBJECTIVE
&fComplete any &e3 of 6&f public upgrades below. Upgrade, link, test, or maintain an existing work; a new build is welcome only when no equivalent exists.
&a&lSTANDARD
&fLeave the result usable by a stranger and record one owner, route, or corrective action. Solo logs and self-audits count.
quests.subtitle: Link what already exists. Make one useful thing survive its first failure.

tasks.title: Read the Public-Works Rubric

quests.title: THE ISLAND REMEMBERS

description: &6&lLORE
&fMirelle circles the map where two old roads nearly meet. She does not ask for another road; she asks for the missing sign, bridge, rail spur, or caretaker that makes the old one dependable.
&e&lOBJECTIVE
&fWALK-THROUGH: Upgrade, link, test, or maintain an existing route, rail, path, or Via Romana line between two useful locations; mark both endpoints and the signage.
&fEXISTING BUILDS COUNT: An existing road, bridge, rail spur, path, or Via Romana line counts when its endpoints, signs, and maintenance owner are made usable.
&fSOLO AUDIT: Walk endpoint-to-endpoint, take one deliberate wrong turn, verify the signs recover the route, and log the caretaker plus one correction.
&a&lSTANDARD
&fAn unbriefed traveller can identify both endpoints, follow the signs, and find the maintenance owner. A solo player may log and correct one navigation failure.
quests.subtitle: Link two useful places and prove the link survives a wrong turn.

tasks.title: Carry a rail marker or route token
REVIEW: Route survives a wrong turn and has a named caretaker

quests.title: CONNECTED ROUTE

description: &6&lLORE
&fElias finds Greybridge's oldest contract written on the back of a receipt. Mirelle calls it proof that markets need rules. Elias calls it proof that rules need somewhere public to be read.
&e&lOBJECTIVE
&fLIVE SERVICE: Upgrade an existing market, stall, contract board, or trade room into a public hall with three active offers or services, visible terms, and one tested transaction.
&fEXISTING BUILDS COUNT: An existing market, stall, contract board, or trade room counts when neutral access, a steward, and readable terms are added or repaired.
&fSOLO AUDIT: Perform and log one transaction from a posted offer, including its price or terms, outcome, and one corrected rule or confusing sign.
&a&lSTANDARD
&fNeutral access, visible terms, and a named steward are present. A solo player may perform and log a test transaction or correct one confusing rule.
quests.subtitle: Turn an existing stall into a place where terms survive the seller.

tasks.title: Place a market token for review
REVIEW: Three active services and a readable public contract

quests.title: MARKET AND CONTRACT HALL

description: &6&lLORE
&fThe workshop survived because somebody labelled one chest. The depot failed because nobody labelled the second.
&fNessa asks for an upgrade joining machine access, repair stock, and a clear line between public and personal tools.
&e&lOBJECTIVE
&fMACHINE TEST: Substantially upgrade an existing workshop or depot so two useful capabilities, a process or repair test, and public/private stock boundaries are obvious.
&fEXISTING BUILDS COUNT: An existing workshop, machine room, tool wall, or depot counts when two capabilities and their public/private stock are labelled and maintained.
&fSOLO AUDIT: Run one processing or repair job start-to-finish, record the result or failure, and correct one broken step, label, or stock boundary.
&a&lSTANDARD
&fTwo capabilities work, operating rules are visible, and a maintainer is named. A solo player may run a repair or processing test and record one corrected failure.
quests.subtitle: Make the useful tools reachable without making them mysteriously vanish.

tasks.title: Bring an andesite-alloy workshop token
REVIEW: Two useful capabilities work and stock boundaries are clear

quests.title: SHARED WORKSHOP AND DEPOT

description: &6&lLORE
&fGreybridge kept three accounts of the same night and trusted none. Elias wants five verifiable memories a later player can compare.
&fMirelle insists the record must also admit what remains uncertain.
&e&lOBJECTIVE
&fSOURCE CHECK: Upgrade an existing archive, map room, memorial, museum, or gallery with five verifiable world facts, their sources, and a place for the sixth.
&fEXISTING BUILDS COUNT: An existing archive, map room, memorial, museum, or gallery counts when its records are browseable, located or dated, and open to a source audit.
&fSOLO AUDIT: Select one entry, trace it to its source, record the fact and uncertainty or correction, and add the audit to the archive log.
&a&lSTANDARD
&fThe facts are browseable, dated or located, and include one uncertainty or correction. A solo player may audit one entry and add its source.
quests.subtitle: Leave the next witness more than your version of events.

tasks.title: Bring a writable archive token
REVIEW: Five sourced memories and one correction are browseable

quests.title: ARCHIVE AND MEMORIAL

description: &6&lLORE
&fGreybridge's refuge was large enough on paper and full enough in practice. Mirelle asks for capacity that can be counted, while Elias asks for an exit that can be found when the lamps are out.
&e&lOBJECTIVE
&fDRILL: Upgrade an existing refuge, alarm point, lit retreat, or emergency station and run a capacity, exit, supplies, and evacuation test.
&fEXISTING BUILDS COUNT: An existing refuge, alarm point, lit retreat, or emergency station counts when its capacity is counted, supplies are ready, and an exit route is marked.
&fSOLO AUDIT: Start at the alarm point, time a simulated evacuation to the refuge and its exit, count usable places and supplies, then sign the maintenance log with one correction.
&a&lSTANDARD
&fThe station is findable under pressure and one failure is corrected. A solo player may self-audit the route and sign the maintenance log.
quests.subtitle: Test the shelter before the island tests it for you.

tasks.title: Carry a readiness lantern

description: &6&lLORE

&fHOSTED TEST: Upgrade an existing dock, hangar, vehicle depot, meeting room, stage, or event ground into one usable public arrival-and-gathering space, then test arrival and one venue function.
&fEXISTING BUILDS COUNT: An existing dock, hangar, vehicle depot, meeting room, stage, or event ground counts when its safe approach and public function are marked and usable.
&fSOLO AUDIT: Arrive by the marked approach, run one event or venue function end-to-end, record the attendance or result, and correct one access or safety failure.
&a&lSTANDARD
&fMark a safe approach, provide one useful vehicle or venue function, and host or self-audit one event/test with a recorded correction.

&fArchive two event results, the cleanup status, one concrete moment, and one unresolved question or change for next time.
&9&lSUITABILITY
&fSolo: record audit | Group: shared archive | Build: book, signs, map wall, or archive chest.
&a&lEVENT STANDARD
&fUse a book, signs, map wall, or archive chest that a late player can find. The archive is reachable without the skirmish; no PvP result is required.
quests.subtitle: [CAPSTONE] After any two safe formats, leave a useful record.

tasks.title: Archive Two Results and One Open Question

quests.title: [CAPSTONE] ARCHIVE THE NIGHT

description: &6&lLORE
&fGreybridge's truce collapsed during a public demonstration. Mirelle Voss and Elias Rook still describe the same bell differently; Nessa Quill archived both versions.
&e&lOBJECTIVE

&fChoose a venue, post the invitation, name hosts and cleanup owners, and display the bell fragment, demonstration ledger, route map, or two witness notes without pretending the contradiction is solved.
&9&lSUITABILITY
&fSolo: staged preparation audit | Group: host the fair | Build: venue, stations, and archive display.
&a&lEVENT STANDARD

&fThe preferred fair has visitors and shared stations. A solo preparation audit may use a staged venue, signed hosting plan, and NPC-facing invitation. The six contributions are alternatives; any three complete the fair.
quests.subtitle: [EVENT] Set one place, one time, and one unresolved history on the table.

tasks.title: Post the Fair Plan and Evidence

quests.title: [EVENT] CALL THE FAIR

description: &4&lLORE
&fMirelle's host book lists a bloodless toast beside the bell fragment: ‘We remember differently; sit anyway.’
&e&lOBJECTIVE
&fHost a Vampire's Delight table, night-route tour, ritual study, archive reading, or aesthetic exhibit.
&9&lSUITABILITY
&fSolo: staged hospitality audit | Group: host guests | Build: table, exhibit, or route stop.
&a&lEVENT STANDARD
&fFor the fair, guests participate safely and leave with one remembered detail. For a solo audit, stage the table or exhibit, sign the guest protocol, and record the intended audience or NPC visitor.
quests.subtitle: [EVENT] Give the night a table without asking for allegiance.

tasks.title: Stage Hospitality and a Guest Record

quests.title: [EVENT] HOUSE HOSPITALITY

description: &b&lLORE
&fElias's margin note says the bell was safe only after somebody explained the exit. The Lantern Order turns that note into a public ward lesson.
&e&lOBJECTIVE
&fHost a safety demonstration, route briefing, rescue drill, countermeasure museum, or support station.
&9&lSUITABILITY
&fSolo: signed test log | Group: teach visitors | Build: support station or marked lesson space.
&a&lEVENT STANDARD
&fFor the fair, visitors can practice or learn without being targets. For a solo audit, stage the display against the environment and sign a test log with expected and observed results.
quests.subtitle: [EVENT] Explain a danger before it becomes a spectacle.

tasks.title: Run a Public Safety Demonstration

quests.title: [EVENT] LANTERN SERVICE

description: &a&lLORE
&fNessa's archive calls the first neutral desk a place where both bell accounts could be delivered without changing hands.
&e&lOBJECTIVE
&fOperate a market, contract desk, courier service, map desk, guesthouse, mediation table, or event logistics station.
&9&lSUITABILITY
&fSolo: documented service test | Group: run one interaction | Build: neutral desk, guesthouse, or logistics station.
&a&lEVENT STANDARD
&fFor the fair, publish terms and complete one real interaction. For a solo audit, post the terms, complete a documented service or route test, and leave the desk ready for a visitor.
quests.subtitle: [EVENT] Make one neutral service actually useful.

tasks.title: Operate One Neutral Service

quests.title: [EVENT] FREE COMPANY MARKET

description: &6&lLORE
&fThe demonstration ledger has a missing line where the bell should have been tested. The workshop fills that gap with an operator, a spectator line, and a failure note.
&e&lOBJECTIVE
&fDemonstrate a Create system, vehicle, dock, rail feature, workshop, or controlled engineering test.
&9&lSUITABILITY
&fSolo: controlled test log | Group: explain and run it | Build: marked workshop, dock, or machine exhibit.
&a&lEVENT STANDARD
&fFor the fair, explain the system and run it once with marked zones. For a solo audit, stage the display, run the test, and sign the expected result, observed result, and repair hook.
quests.subtitle: [EVENT] Let one machine explain itself before it moves.

tasks.title: Run a Controlled Machine Demonstration

quests.title: [EVENT] ENGINEERING EXHIBITION

description: &e&lLORE
&fA witness remembered the bell by the sound of the crowd afterward. The fair keeps that human detail: a game, ceremony, music cue, or guided tour that ends with someone taking part.
&e&lOBJECTIVE
&fRun a performance, mini-game, ceremony, award, speech, guided tour, or other shared activity.
&9&lSUITABILITY
&fSolo: staged test run | Group: participate together | Build: stage, game lane, or tour route.
&a&lEVENT STANDARD
&fFor the fair, announce how to join and show a visible ending. For a solo audit, stage the activity, write the joining instructions, and record a test run or NPC audience response.
quests.subtitle: [EVENT] Give visitors a reason to participate.

tasks.title: Run a Participatory Showcase

quests.title: [EVENT] PUBLIC SHOWCASE

description: &f&lLORE
&fThe archive does not choose between Mirelle and Elias. It preserves the bell fragment, both witness notes, the demonstration ledger, and the route that led people home.
&e&lOBJECTIVE
&fPreserve five concrete season facts, images, maps, quotes, results, or failures and identify one unfinished hook.
&9&lSUITABILITY
&fSolo: signed archive audit | Group: browse and contribute | Build: durable archive with next-page marker.
&a&lEVENT STANDARD
&fFor the fair, make the record browseable for a late player. For a solo audit, sign and file the five entries in a durable archive with a clearly marked next page.
quests.subtitle: [EVENT] Preserve five facts and leave one door open.

tasks.title: File Five Season Facts

quests.title: [EVENT] ARCHIVE THE SEASON

description: &6&lLORE
&fAt the fair's last bell, Mirelle and Elias still disagree. Nessa's blank page is not an invitation to invent a clean answer; it is a promise that the next season may examine the evidence.
&e&lOBJECTIVE
&fComplete any three fair contributions and record one unresolved pressure or ambition that players genuinely want to continue.
&6&lSEASON SEAL REWARDS
&f3 personal Bevels + personal fair favor + team festival support. No currency is added to reward table #9.
&9&lSUITABILITY
&fSolo: staged seal audit | Group: gather at the fair | Build: capstone venue and sequel-hook archive.
&a&lEVENT STANDARD
&fThe preferred capstone is a real public gathering. A solo seal audit must point to three staged contribution records and one signed sequel hook; it does not pretend a crowd attended.
quests.subtitle: [CAPSTONE] Complete any three contributions, then name what remains unresolved.

tasks.title: Seal the Fair and Leave a Future Hook

quests.title: [CAPSTONE] SEAL SEASON ONE

description: &f&lLORE
&fNessa's final note leaves the two bell accounts side by side. The fair is over; the disagreement is now part of the island's usable history.
&e&lOBJECTIVE
&fPlace the fair record and one genuine future hook in the public archive, then leave a writable page or clearly marked place for the next entry.
&9&lSUITABILITY
&fSolo: findability audit | Group: announce the archive | Build: public record wall or writable archive.
&a&lEVENT STANDARD
&fFor a group, announce where the record lives. For a solo audit, verify that a new player can find and understand it without an oral briefing.
quests.subtitle: [EVENT] Put the final record somewhere the next season can find it.

tasks.title: File the Fair's Final Record
REVIEW: Record One Contradiction, Success, and Future Promise

quests.title: [EVENT] ARCHIVE AFTERMATH

description: {image:numismatics:textures/item/coin/bevel.png width:48 height:48 align:center}
&6&lROUTE · DELIVERY · PUBLIC DESTINATION
&7&lLORE:&f The Atlas closes the season ledger after the seal. Nessa Quill keeps the post-season courier route open, carrying useful caches to places the island already uses.
&e&lOBJECTIVE:&f Choose a public service, name its route and destination, and agree who will receive and place the team cache.
&a&lSTANDARD:&f Submit the visible Bevel price only after the payer, delivery route, public destination, and handoff owner are written down. Each paid service renews after seven days.
quests.subtitle: Post-season services for routes and public destinations the island actually uses.

tasks.title: Read the Civic Requisition Terms

quests.title: AFTER THE BELLS

description: &7&lLORE:&f A festival works when the supplies reach the public square before the first bell, not when they remain in a private chest.
&e&lOBJECTIVE:&f Submit 1 Bevel for 16 Firework Rockets and 8 Lanterns.
&9&lUTILITY TAGS:&f [ROUTE] [DELIVERY] [PUBLIC DESTINATION]
&a&lSTANDARD:&f Name the event route, public destination, delivery owner, and safe handoff point before claiming the team cache.
quests.subtitle: Fireworks and lanterns delivered to a named public event route.

quests.title: [DELIVERY] FESTIVAL CACHE — 1 BEVEL

description: &4&lLORE:&f The first welcome after Greybridge is deliberately ordinary: a guest needs a findable room, a readable promise, and enough light to leave safely.
&e&lOBJECTIVE:&f Submit 1 Bevel for 8 Books and 8 Lanterns.
&9&lUTILITY TAGS:&f [ROUTE] [DELIVERY] [PUBLIC DESTINATION]
&a&lSTANDARD:&f Name the public hall, guesthouse, archive, or refuge, then record the delivery owner and the route a visitor can follow to the handoff.
quests.subtitle: Books and lanterns for a shared guest space or civic hall.

description: {image:minecraft:textures/item/writable_book.png width:48 height:48 align:center}
&f&lTRUST DISPATCH
&7&lLORE:&f Nessa Quill keeps a spare courier line for civic problems that have a place to begin. The dispatch must concern the island being built now, not a required return to Greybridge.
&e&lOBJECTIVE:&f File one short dispatch naming a real in-world location and the concrete problem found there.
&e&lACTION:&f State one useful action another player can take next session, then name the owner responsible for receiving or closing the dispatch.
&a&lSTANDARD:&f A trust checkmark is enough: the entry is specific, findable, and actionable. This renews every 604800 seconds and grants exactly 1 team Bevel; it consumes no Bevel.
quests.subtitle: One real location, one problem, one action, one owner — exactly one team Bevel weekly.

tasks.title: I Added One Actionable Rumour

quests.title: FILE A CIVIC DISPATCH

description: {image:minecraft:textures/item/filled_map.png width:48 height:48 align:center}
&e&lPUBLIC DESTINATION FILE
&7&lLORE:&f Nessa will carry one pressure forward, but she will not invent a destination for people who have already moved on. The old Greybridge failure is context, not a live-world prerequisite.
&e&lOBJECTIVE:&f Record one unresolved pressure, its public destination, stakeholders, evidence, and the practical route by which players can inspect it.
&a&lSTANDARD:&f Add one concrete future action and a named owner or steward; keep the hook useful without inventing a required location.
quests.subtitle: Leave a public destination, stakeholders, and a reason to return.
